original_english: It is widely accepted amongst the scientific community that life originated in water.
hinglish_roman: Scientific community mein yeh widely accept kiya jaata hai ki life ki utpatti paani mein hui thi.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: Some researchers believe that life may have originated in small water pools with changing environmental conditions rather than in the oceans.
hinglish_roman: Kuch researchers ka maanna hai ki life oceans ki bajaye chote paani ke pools mein originate hui hogi jahan environmental conditions badlati rehti thi.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: Hot springs in Puga Valley in Ladakh maintain very high temperatures even in a cold climate.
hinglish_roman: Ladakh ke Puga Valley ke hot springs thande climate mein bhi bahut zyada temperature maintain karte hain.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: The organisms living in these hot springs are mostly heat-loving bacteria called thermophiles, which are unicellular.
hinglish_roman: Inn hot springs mein rehne wale organisms mostly heat-loving bacteria hote hain jinhe thermophiles kaha jaata hai, aur yeh unicellular hote hain.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: Calcium carbonate formed rapidly around hot springs and may have helped in the formation of the first protective membrane.
hinglish_roman: Hot springs ke aas-paas calcium carbonate tezi se banta tha aur shayad pehli protective membrane ke formation mein madad ki hogi.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: All living organisms are made up of cells and the cell represents the basic level at which life exists.
hinglish_roman: Saare living organisms cells se bane hote hain aur cell woh basic level hai jahan life exist karti hai.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: Some organisms like bacteria or yeast consist of only one cell and are called unicellular organisms.
hinglish_roman: Bacteria ya yeast jaise kuch organisms sirf ek cell se milkar bane hote hain aur inhe unicellular organisms kaha jaata hai.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: Plants, fish, birds, or humans are made up of millions of cells that work together and are called multicellular organisms.
hinglish_roman: Paudhe, machhliyan, pakshi ya insaan millions of cells se milkar bane hote hain jo ek saath kaam karte hain, inhe multicellular organisms kehte hain.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: A group of similar cells performing similar functions forms tissues.
hinglish_roman: Ek jaisi functions karne wale similar cells ka group milkar tissue banaata hai.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: Different tissues are organised to form an organ and several organs work together to form organ systems.
hinglish_roman: Alag-alag tissues milkar ek organ banate hain aur kai organs milkar organ system banaate hain.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: The limit of resolution of the human eye is 0.1 mm, meaning two points closer than this appear as a single point.
hinglish_roman: Human eye ki resolution limit 0.1 mm hoti hai, matlab agar do points isse zyada paas hon toh woh ek single point lagte hain.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: Robert Hooke was the first person to observe a cell in 1665 using a self-designed microscope.
hinglish_roman: Robert Hooke ne 1665 mein apne banaye hue microscope se pehli baar cell observe kiya tha.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: While examining a thin slice of cork, Hooke observed small box-like compartments and named them cells.
hinglish_roman: Cork ki얇i slice examine karte waqt Hooke ne chote box-jaisi compartments dekhi aur unhe cells naam diya.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: Scientists improved the microscope by improving its three main features — resolution, contrast, and magnification.
hinglish_roman: Scientists ne microscope ko uske teen main features — resolution, contrast, aur magnification — ko improve karke behtar banaya.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: Electron microscopes use a beam of electrons instead of light to produce highly magnified images at the nanometre scale.
hinglish_roman: Electron microscopes light ki jagah electrons ki beam use karte hain aur nanometre scale par highly magnified images produce karte hain.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: The cell membrane is a thin boundary that surrounds a cell and protects its contents.
hinglish_roman: Cell membrane ek patli boundary hoti hai jo cell ko gherta hai aur uske contents ki suraksha karti hai.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: The cell membrane is selectively permeable, which means it allows some substances to pass through it while blocking others.
hinglish_roman: Cell membrane selectively permeable hoti hai, yaani yeh kuch substances ko andar aane deti hai aur doosron ko rok deti hai.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: Osmosis is the movement of water through a selectively permeable membrane from a region of lower solute concentration to higher solute concentration.
hinglish_roman: Osmosis ek aisi process hai jisme paani selectively permeable membrane ke zariye kam solute concentration wali jagah se zyada solute concentration wali jagah ki taraf move karta hai.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: Diffusion is the net movement of particles from a higher to a lower concentration even without a membrane.
hinglish_roman: Diffusion mein particles bina membrane ke bhi zyada concentration wali jagah se kam concentration wali jagah ki taraf move karte hain.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: The cell membrane is made up of lipids and proteins and is about 7 to 10 nanometres thick.
hinglish_roman: Cell membrane lipids aur proteins se bani hoti hai aur iska thickness lagbhag 7 se 10 nanometres hota hai.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: The fluid-mosaic model explains that the membrane has a lipid bilayer with proteins embedded in it.
hinglish_roman: Fluid-mosaic model yeh explain karta hai ki membrane mein ek lipid bilayer hota hai jisme proteins embedded hote hain.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: In the lipid bilayer, the water-attracting heads face outward and the water-repelling tails face inward.
hinglish_roman: Lipid bilayer mein paani ko attract karne wale heads bahar ki taraf hote hain aur paani ko repel karne wale tails andar ki taraf hote hain.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: Plant, fungi, and bacteria cells have an additional layer called the cell wall outside the cell membrane.
hinglish_roman: Paudhon, fungi, aur bacteria ke cells mein cell membrane ke bahar ek aur layer hoti hai jise cell wall kehte hain.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: The plant cell wall is primarily made of cellulose, a type of carbohydrate formed by many glucose units linked together.
hinglish_roman: Plant cell wall mainly cellulose se bani hoti hai, jo ek tarah ka carbohydrate hai jo kaafi glucose units ke aapas mein jude hone se banta hai.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: When a plant cell is placed in a concentrated sugar solution, the inner content shrinks while the cell wall maintains the outer shape.
hinglish_roman: Jab plant cell ko concentrated sugar solution mein rakha jaata hai, toh andar ka content shrink kar jaata hai lekin cell wall bahar ka shape maintain karti hai.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: Animal cells do not have a cell wall, so they can change shape easily and support tissue movement.
hinglish_roman: Animal cells mein cell wall nahi hoti, isliye woh aasaani se shape change kar sakti hain aur tissue movement mein madad karti hain.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: A bacterial cell lacks a well-defined nucleus and membrane-bound organelles and is called a prokaryotic cell.
hinglish_roman: Bacterial cell mein well-defined nucleus aur membrane-bound organelles nahi hote, aur ise prokaryotic cell kaha jaata hai.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: Plant and animal cells have a well-defined nucleus and several membrane-bound organelles and are called eukaryotic cells.
hinglish_roman: Plant aur animal cells mein well-defined nucleus aur kaafi membrane-bound organelles hote hain, inhe eukaryotic cells kehte hain.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: The nucleus has a double-layered covering called the nuclear membrane, which has pores that allow material transfer between the nucleus and the cytoplasm.
hinglish_roman: Nucleus ke upar double-layered covering hoti hai jise nuclear membrane kehte hain, isme pores hote hain jo nucleus aur cytoplasm ke beech material transfer allow karte hain.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: The nucleolus is the dense round body in the nucleus where synthesis of ribosomal subunits takes place.
hinglish_roman: Nucleolus nucleus ke andar ek ghani golaakar structure hoti hai jahan ribosomal subunits ka synthesis hota hai.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: Chromosomes contain information for inheritance of characters from parents to the next generation in the form of DNA molecules.
hinglish_roman: Chromosomes mein DNA molecules ke roop mein genetic information hoti hai jo parents se next generation ko milti hai.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: The functional segments of DNA are called genes and they carry genetic information.
hinglish_roman: DNA ke functional segments ko genes kehte hain aur yeh genetic information carry karte hain.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: Mature Red Blood Cells in humans do not have a nucleus, which provides more space for haemoglobin to carry oxygen.
hinglish_roman: Insano mein mature Red Blood Cells mein nucleus nahi hota, jis wajah se haemoglobin ke liye zyada jagah milti hai aur woh zyada oxygen carry kar sakti hai.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: Ribosomes are tiny structures that may be present freely in the cytoplasm or attached to the endoplasmic reticulum and are the sites of protein synthesis.
hinglish_roman: Ribosomes choti structures hoti hain jo cytoplasm mein freely ya endoplasmic reticulum se attached ho sakti hain aur protein synthesis ka kaam karti hain.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: The Endoplasmic Reticulum is a large organelle that spreads like a network within the cytoplasm.
hinglish_roman: Endoplasmic Reticulum ek bada organelle hai jo cytoplasm ke andar ek network ki tarah failaa hota hai.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: Rough Endoplasmic Reticulum has ribosomes on its surface and is mainly involved in protein synthesis and secretion.
hinglish_roman: Rough Endoplasmic Reticulum ki surface par ribosomes hote hain aur yeh mainly protein synthesis aur secretion mein involved hoti hai.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: Smooth Endoplasmic Reticulum does not have ribosomes and is involved in the synthesis and storage of fats and hormones.
hinglish_roman: Smooth Endoplasmic Reticulum mein ribosomes nahi hote aur yeh fats aur hormones ke synthesis aur storage mein kaam aati hai.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: The Golgi apparatus modifies, sorts, and packages proteins and lipids into vesicles for transport or secretion.
hinglish_roman: Golgi apparatus proteins aur lipids ko modify, sort aur package karke vesicles mein daalata hai taaki unhe transport ya secrete kiya ja sake.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: Lysosomes are single membrane-bound sacs filled with enzymes that break down unwanted proteins, carbohydrates, and fats.
hinglish_roman: Lysosomes single membrane se ghire hue sacs hote hain jinme enzymes bhari hoti hain jo unwanted proteins, carbohydrates aur fats ko tod deti hain.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: Mitochondria are called the powerhouses of the cell because they supply energy needed for most cellular activities.
hinglish_roman: Mitochondria ko cell ka powerhouse kaha jaata hai kyunki yeh zyaadatar cellular activities ke liye zaruri energy supply karte hain.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: Each mitochondrion is surrounded by two membranes, with the inner membrane folded into cristae to increase surface area.
hinglish_roman: Har ek mitochondrion do membranes se ghira hota hai, jisme inner membrane cristae mein fold hoti hai taaki surface area badh sake.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: In mitochondria, glucose is broken down during cellular respiration and energy is stored as ATP.
hinglish_roman: Mitochondria mein cellular respiration ke dauran glucose toot ta hai aur energy ATP ke roop mein store hoti hai.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: ATP acts as the energy currency of the cell and is used for most cellular activities.
hinglish_roman: ATP cell ki energy currency ki tarah kaam karta hai aur zyaadatar cellular activities ke liye use hota hai.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: Plastids are special organelles in plant cells used for food synthesis and storage.
hinglish_roman: Plastids plant cells mein special organelles hote hain jo food synthesis aur storage ke liye use hote hain.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: Chloroplasts contain a green pigment called chlorophyll that absorbs sunlight for photosynthesis.
hinglish_roman: Chloroplasts mein chlorophyll naam ka green pigment hota hai jo photosynthesis ke liye sunlight absorb karta hai.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: Chloroplasts are double-membrane-bound organelles and contain a semi-fluid substance called stroma.
hinglish_roman: Chloroplasts double-membrane se ghire organelles hote hain aur inke andar stroma naam ka semi-fluid substance hota hai.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: Chromoplasts are plastids that contain pigments like yellow, orange, or red and are responsible for bright colours in flowers and fruits.
hinglish_roman: Chromoplasts woh plastids hain jinme yellow, orange ya red jaisi pigments hoti hain aur yeh phoolon aur phalon ke bright colours ke liye zimmedaar hote hain.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: Leucoplasts are colourless plastids that store food material such as starch, oils, or proteins.
hinglish_roman: Leucoplasts rangheen nahi hote, yeh colourless plastids hote hain jo starch, oils ya proteins jaisa food store karte hain.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: Mitochondria and plastids have their own DNA and ribosomes suggesting they share an evolutionary history with bacteria.
hinglish_roman: Mitochondria aur plastids ke paas apna DNA aur ribosomes hote hain, jo yeh suggest karta hai ki inका bacteria ke saath evolutionary connection raha hoga.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: In a mature plant cell, there is usually one large central vacuole surrounded by a selectively permeable membrane filled with cell sap.
hinglish_roman: Ek mature plant cell mein aam taur par ek bada central vacuole hota hai jo selectively permeable membrane se ghira hota hai aur cell sap se bhara hota hai.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: The vacuole stores water, minerals, sugars, and waste material and helps maintain pressure inside the cell.
hinglish_roman: Vacuole mein paani, minerals, sugars aur waste material store hota hai aur yeh cell ke andar pressure maintain karne mein madad karta hai.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: When a plant does not get enough water, the vacuole loses water and the plant gets wilted.
hinglish_roman: Jab paudhe ko paafi paani nahi milta, toh vacuole paani kho deta hai aur paudha murjha jaata hai.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: In eukaryotic cells, a network of fine fibres forms the cytoskeleton which provides structural support and enables cell movement.
hinglish_roman: Eukaryotic cells mein fine fibres ka ek network hota hai jise cytoskeleton kehte hain, yeh structural support deta hai aur cell movement mein bhi madad karta hai.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: Cell division is the process by which new cells are formed from pre-existing cells.
hinglish_roman: Cell division woh process hai jisme naye cells pehle se existing cells se bante hain.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: Cell division allows living organisms to grow, repair damaged tissues, and reproduce.
hinglish_roman: Cell division ki wajah se living organisms grow kar sakte hain, damaged tissues repair ho sakti hain aur reproduction bhi hota hai.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: Mitosis produces two genetically identical daughter cells from one parent cell with the same number of chromosomes.
hinglish_roman: Mitosis mein ek parent cell se do genetically identical daughter cells bante hain jinme chromosomes ki same sankhya hoti hai.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: Mitosis is important for normal growth, repair, maintenance, and asexual reproduction.
hinglish_roman: Mitosis normal growth, repair, maintenance aur asexual reproduction ke liye zaroori hai.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: Meiosis is a type of cell division that produces gametes and occurs only in the cells of reproductive organs.
hinglish_roman: Meiosis ek aisi cell division hai jo gametes produce karti hai aur sirf reproductive organs ki cells mein hoti hai.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: In meiosis, the parent cell divides twice to form four daughter cells, each having half the number of chromosomes.
hinglish_roman: Meiosis mein parent cell do baar divide hoti hai aur chaar daughter cells banti hain, jinme se har ek mein chromosomes ki adhi sankhya hoti hai.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: During fertilisation, when gametes from two individuals combine, the original chromosome number is restored.
hinglish_roman: Fertilisation ke dauran jab do individuals ke gametes aapas mein milte hain, toh chromosomes ki original sankhya wapas aa jaati hai.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: In 1838, Matthias Schleiden reported that all plants are made up of cells.
hinglish_roman: 1838 mein Matthias Schleiden ne report kiya ki saare paudhe cells se bane hote hain.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: Rudolf Virchow in 1855 stated that new cells are formed only from pre-existing cells.
hinglish_roman: Rudolf Virchow ne 1855 mein kaha ki naye cells sirf pehle se exist karne wale cells se hi bante hain.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: According to the classical Cell Theory, all living organisms are made up of cells, the cell is the basic unit of life, and all cells arise from pre-existing cells.
hinglish_roman: Classical Cell Theory ke mutabiq, saare living organisms cells se bane hain, cell life ki basic unit hai, aur saare cells pehle se exist karne wale cells se hi bante hain.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: Cells grow and divide in a controlled way and eventually die when they are no longer needed.
hinglish_roman: Cells ek controlled tarike se grow aur divide karti hain aur jab inki zaroorat nahi rehti toh yeh mar jaati hain.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: Contact inhibition is the process where cell division stops when cells come in contact with neighbouring cells.
hinglish_roman: Contact inhibition woh process hai jisme cell division ruk jaati hai jab cells apne neighbouring cells se touch karti hain.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: Cancer cells lose contact inhibition and keep dividing uncontrollably, leading to the formation of tumours.
hinglish_roman: Cancer cells contact inhibition kho deti hain aur uncontrollably divide hoti rehti hain, jisse tumour ban jaata hai.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: Programmed Cell Death is a genetically regulated process of selective cell destruction essential for normal development.
hinglish_roman: Programmed Cell Death ek genetically regulated process hai jisme selective cell destruction hoti hai, yeh normal development ke liye zaroori hai.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: Errors in mitosis can lead to uncontrolled cell division, resulting in tumours and abnormal chromosome numbers.
hinglish_roman: Mitosis mein galtiyan hone se uncontrolled cell division ho sakti hai, jisse tumours aur abnormal chromosome numbers ki samsya aa sakti hai.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: Errors in meiosis may result in genetic disorders associated with developmental problems or cause early pregnancy loss.
hinglish_roman: Meiosis mein galtiyan genetic disorders ko janm de sakti hain jo developmental problems se judi hoti hain ya phir pregnancy ke shuruaat mein hi loss ka kaaran ban sakti hain.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: Cell culture is the process of growing plant and animal cells outside the body in special nutrient-rich conditions.
hinglish_roman: Cell culture woh process hai jisme plant aur animal cells ko body ke bahar special nutrient-rich conditions mein grow karaya jaata hai.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: J. Craig Venter's team created a synthetic copy of bacterial DNA and inserted it into another bacterium, which then grew following the new DNA's instructions.
hinglish_roman: J. Craig Venter ki team ne ek bacterium ka synthetic DNA copy banaya aur use doosre bacterium mein daal diya, jiske baad woh nayi DNA ki instructions se grow karne laga.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: Gottlieb Haberlandt proposed that any living plant cell can develop into a complete plant if provided with suitable nutrients — a property called totipotency.
hinglish_roman: Gottlieb Haberlandt ne propose kiya ki koi bhi living plant cell agar use suitable nutrients mile toh ek poore paudhe mein develop ho sakti hai, is khaasiyat ko totipotency kehte hain.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: In plants, meiosis occurs in anthers to form pollen grains and in ovaries to produce egg cells.
hinglish_roman: Paudhon mein meiosis anthers mein hoti hai jisse pollen grains bante hain aur ovaries mein hoti hai jisse egg cells banti hain.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: Human sperm cells contain lysosomal enzymes that help break down the outer layer of the egg during fertilisation.
hinglish_roman: Human sperm cells mein lysosomal enzymes hote hain jo fertilisation ke dauran egg ki outer layer ko todne mein madad karte hain.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: Prokaryotic cells have a primitive nucleus called the nucleoid where their genetic material is located without a membrane.
hinglish_roman: Prokaryotic cells mein ek primitive nucleus hota hai jise nucleoid kehte hain, jahan bina kisi membrane ke genetic material hota hai.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: What is osmosis and how is it different from diffusion?
hinglish_roman: Osmosis kya hota hai aur yeh diffusion se kaise alag hai?
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: Can you explain the difference between prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells?
hinglish_roman: Kya aap prokaryotic aur eukaryotic cells ka difference explain kar sakte hain?
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: What is the fluid-mosaic model of the cell membrane?
hinglish_roman: Cell membrane ka fluid-mosaic model kya hota hai?
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: Give me an example of how osmosis works in daily life.
hinglish_roman: Mujhe daily life mein osmosis kaise kaam karta hai iska ek example do.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: What is the definition of mitosis?
hinglish_roman: Mitosis ki definition kya hai?
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: What are the functions of the Golgi apparatus in a cell?
hinglish_roman: Cell mein Golgi apparatus ke kya functions hote hain?
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: How is meiosis different from mitosis? Please compare both.
hinglish_roman: Meiosis aur mitosis mein kya antar hai? Dono ko compare karke batao.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: Can you explain what ATP is and why it is called the energy currency of the cell?
hinglish_roman: ATP kya hota hai aur ise cell ki energy currency kyun kaha jaata hai, explain karo.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: What is the difference between chloroplasts, chromoplasts, and leucoplasts?
hinglish_roman: Chloroplasts, chromoplasts aur leucoplasts mein kya fark hota hai?
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: Give me an example of how the cell wall helps a plant stay upright.
hinglish_roman: Mujhe ek example do ki cell wall kaise paudhe ko seedha khada rehne mein madad karti hai.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: What would happen to a cell if the mitochondria stopped working?
hinglish_roman: Agar cell mein mitochondria kaam karna band kar de toh kya hoga?
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: What is the formula for estimating the size of a cell under a microscope?
hinglish_roman: Microscope ke neeche cell ki size estimate karne ka formula kya hai?
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: Can you explain the concept of contact inhibition and how it prevents tumour formation?
hinglish_roman: Contact inhibition ka concept kya hai aur yeh tumour formation ko kaise rokta hai, explain karo?
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: What is totipotency? Give a real-world example.
hinglish_roman: Totipotency kya hoti hai? Iska ek real-world example bhi do.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: Why do mature red blood cells in humans lack a nucleus?
hinglish_roman: Insano mein mature red blood cells mein nucleus kyun nahi hota?
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: The cell membrane is selectively permeable and allows only some substances to pass through.
hinglish_roman: Cell membrain selecteevly parmiabel hoti hai aur sirf kuch hi substancees ko pass karne deti hai.
hinglish_corrected: Cell membrane selectively permeable hoti hai aur sirf kuch hi substances ko pass karne deti hai.

hinglish_roman: Mitocondria cell ka powerhouse hote hain aur cellular respirashun ke zariye ATP produce karte hain.
hinglish_corrected: Mitochondria cell ka powerhouse hote hain aur cellular respiration ke zariye ATP produce karte hain.

hinglish_roman: Chromosoms DNA aur proteen se bane hote hain aur genetic informashun carry karte hain.
hinglish_corrected: Chromosomes DNA aur proteins se bane hote hain aur genetic information carry karte hain.

original_english: Ribosomes are the sites of protein synthesis in the cell.
hinglish_roman: Ribosoms cell mein protein synthasis ki site hote hain.
hinglish_corrected: Ribosomes cell mein protein synthesis ki site hote hain.

original_english: The nucleus controls all the activities of the cell and contains the genetic material.
hinglish_roman: Nucleas cell ki saari activities control karta hai aur genetic meterial contain karta hai.
hinglish_corrected: Nucleus cell ki saari activities control karta hai aur genetic material contain karta hai.
